title: Vaccine manufacturing surge capacity for pandemics
bottleneck: Global vaccine production is concentrated in a few countries and companies, and scaling from zero to billions of doses takes months even with platform technologies like mRNA. Supply-chain bottlenecks in lipids, vials, and fill-finish capacity constrained the COVID-19 rollout, and little surge capacity has been built since.
why_it_blocks: A vaccine that cannot be manufactured at pandemic scale is a scientific trophy, not a public health tool. Manufacturing, not discovery, was the binding constraint in 2021 and remains so.
current_state: The WHO's 100-day mission aims for vaccines within 100 days of a pandemic threat, with geographically diversified production. mRNA technology-transfer hubs exist in principle but limited commercial-scale capacity in low-income regions. Single-use bioreactor systems and modular fill-finish plants could decentralize production, but capital costs and trained-workforce shortages keep manufacturing concentrated in a few countries.
